decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line that moved from a simple mention in 2023 to its own page in 2024, Product A appears to be performing at least satisfactorily against aspirations and fits the firm's main business.

Product B stayed only as a website mention and is overshadowed by stronger insole offerings, but as a low-resource complement to the footwear range a large firm with slack is still likely to retain it for now.

Product C also shows only limited market prominence and overlaps with other insole solutions, yet the firm's broad accessory strategy and available slack make continued offering slightly more likely than withdrawal.

Product D had its own page in both 2023 and 2024, indicating continued support and results likely above aspiration for an innovation closely aligned with the firm's ergonomic and protective-footwear positioning.
Product E gained visibility from a mention in 2023 to its own page in 2024, suggesting improving acceptance and making retention likely despite being a more specialized niche line.
Product F is a stated flagship shown on the home page in both years and backed by a concrete customer-use result, so management would see little reason to reallocate resources away from it.
